weights_gb_note: decimal GB; bf16 = sum of safetensors sizes on the hub (equals 2 x params); 4bit = NF4 + double-quant estimate: 6.979 B quantisable linear params x 0.5159 B + remaining params in bf16
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: yes (16.06 GB weights; core.batches() sizes batches from free memory); 4bit also possible (~5.7 GB) via adapter.load(quant='4bit') but not needed

hidden_last_long_context.assumes: core.Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats as of SPEC v1: one forward with output_hidden_states=True over a chunk of n prompts (left-padded to T tokens, the longest of the chunk) keeps (num_layers + 1) bf16 hidden states [n, T, hidden] and all-position logits [n, T, vocab], plus a KV cache (use_cache defaults to True; gb_kv_cache_upper_bound assumes full attention in every layer: exact for Llama, an over-estimate for Gemma's 5:1 sliding-window layers); the gb_* figures of the longest prompt are the n = 1 case; transient activations and allocator overhead are NOT counted, so the real need is higher
hidden_last_long_context.prompt_set: sbx.evals.get_pool()['hard'] (281 questions after the sbx.evals prompt-length cap MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500, 296 before it; sbx/dirs/sandbag.py:sandbag_hard calls ctx.hidden_last on all of them), framing E, meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tokenizer (same vocab / merges / template as 3.3-70B)
hidden_last_long_context.verdict_rule: fits_80gb = gb_peak_upper_bound <= 0.9 * 85 (an '80 GB' A100/H100 has ~85e9 bytes; 10% headroom, the same rule as for the weights); a 'false' verdict additionally needs gb_peak_lower_bound > 0.9 * 85, i.e. it does not depend on the KV-cache term. Arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU

largest_chunk.basis: Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats forward chunks of prompts, not single prompts: core.batches() packs the prompts, shortest first, into chunks of at most tok_budget = 14000 padded prompt tokens (prompts x the longest prompt of the chunk; only a single prompt above the budget makes a bigger chunk) and that budget does not depend on the model or on the free memory, so the memory peak is set by the biggest chunk. The figures for the longest prompt alone underestimate it whenever that prompt is shorter than the budget, which holds for every pooled prompt since the sbx.evals prompt cap. tokens = max(tok_budget, longest_prompt_tokens) is an upper bound on the padded tokens of one chunk (a smaller prefill or KV budget on a small GPU can make the real chunks smaller); the sizes are the same formulas as above at that many tokens
largest_chunk.verdict_rule: fits = gb_peak_upper_bound <= 0.9 * 85; does not fit = gb_peak_lower_bound > 0.9 * 85 (independent of the KV-cache term); borderline = in between (the lower bound is below the 90% line, the upper bound is above it). Same thresholds as fits_80gb above. Arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (200/302 = accessible, 403 = gated and access not granted)

min_transformers_note: llama3 rope scaling landed in 4.43.0 (Llama-3.1); only 4.57.6 was actually run here

layer_path_verified.method: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(real hub config) under accelerate.init_empty_weights (meta device) + tie_weights(); numerics of the 1-based convention on a tiny random model of the same HF class (sbx/tests/test_adapters_gemma_llama.py)
layer_path_verified.convention: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] for 1 <= L < nl (exact); hidden_states[nl] is post final norm (avoid L = nl)

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured mean over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option questions) with the real tokenizer + adapter.build; the long-context sets are longer but bounded by the sbx.evals prompt-length cap (MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500): every question served by sbx.evals builds a framing-E prompt of at most 2,892 tokens (a GPQA-bio question) and the LAB-Bench sets average ~0.7k (labbench_seqqa), ~1.2k (labbench_protocolqa) and ~1.6k (labbench_cloning, 6 questions left) tokens with framing N; the raw LAB-Bench files have prompts of up to 51k characters (docs/evals.md section 3)

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE of generated tokens per 4-option bio MCQ under the cot prompt (prior knowledge of how verbose these models are); NOT measured (no weights available locally). Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run; max_new=512 truncates longer answers (they count as unparsed).
template_notes:
Chat template (3.1-8B and the official 3.3-70B tokenizer_config are the same string, sha256 e10ca381b1ccc5cf; vocab and merges identical): '<|begin_of_text|>' + ALWAYS a system header '<|start_header_id|>system<|end_header_id|>

Cutting Knowledge Date: December 2023
Today Date: {date_string}

{system}<|eot_id|>' (even with no system message), then '<|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>

{user}<|eot_id|>'; generation prompt '<|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>

'. The 3.1/3.3 template defaults the date to the fixed '26 Jul 2024' (verified); a variant defaulting to strftime_now() (I believe Llama-3.2-style templates do; not checked) would make prompts depend on the day, so render() always passes date_string='26 Jul 2024' explicitly (the tests build such a variant to prove it). Framing text goes in the system role after the date lines (sys_role='system'). BOS comes from the template; Adapter.encode uses add_special_tokens=False -> exactly one BOS. Generation stops at eos ids [128001, 128008, 128009]; decoded text ends with '<|eot_id|>' then pad tokens.
known_issues: Tokenizer has no pad token: adapter.load() sets '<|finetune_right_pad_id|>' (not the eos/eot token) and left padding.
N prompts already contain a system turn (the date header); there is no 'no system prompt' variant in the Llama format.
Often finishes with 'The final answer is: $\boxed{X}$' instead of 'Answer: X'; parse_letter handles both.
Shipped generation_config has temperature=0.6/top_p=0.9 with do_sample=True; core passes do_sample=False (greedy), HF prints a harmless warning.
Not run on real weights (none available locally): max_new, est_tokens_per_question and output formats are unmeasured; mechanics were verified on a tiny random LlamaForCausalLM.
recommended_gpu: 1 x 24 GB (L4 / A10 / RTX 4090) in bf16 (16.1 GB weights, small batches); 40-80 GB for large batches. Direction building (core.Ctx.hidden_last) needs ~17-18 GB for the longest pooled prompt (2,272 tokens) and ~23-25 GB for the largest chunk core.batches() builds (14,000 padded prompt tokens), see hidden_last_long_context: a 24 GB card is not enough for the chunk, use 40 GB or more for it (arithmetic, NOT run on a GPU).
download_gb_note: sum of the bf16 safetensors shards (plus a few MB of tokenizer/config files)

special_tokens.pad_note: set by Llama3.load() (3.1 ships without a pad token; the official 3.3 tokenizer already has it)
special_tokens.generation_eos_source: generation_config.json (3.1-8B official; the 3.3 mirror's generation_config.json has the same list)
